questions: Should the chosen number of black balls equal the chosen number of white balls exactly, or can it be any non-zero equal count? (i.e., is zero allowed?)
If multiple choices yield the same maximum sum, should we output that sum (just the maximum), or is there a different selection rule?
Are we allowed to choose balls in any order, or is the selection just a subset without regard to sequence?
Should we maximize the sum of values, or simply compute the sum for some arbitrary equal-count choice?
Can we choose the same ball more than once? (i.e., is selection with replacement allowed?)
If N != M, is the maximum possible equal count min(N, M), or can we choose any k ≤ min(N, M)?
Are the balls distinguishable only by value, or are indices relevant for uniqueness?
Should the output be the maximum sum, or the sum for the choice that also minimizes something else if sums tie?
